description: Internet-Facing Application Load Balancer without a Web ACL
rationale: An internet-facing application load balancer answers every request that reaches its DNS name, and passes it to the targets behind it. Nothing between the internet and the application inspects that request unless a WAF web ACL is associated with the load balancer: the security groups decide which ports answer, not what is sent to them. Without an ACL the injection payloads, the path traversal attempts and the volume a single source can send are all handled by the application itself, and the account has no record of them.
remediation: Associate a WAF web ACL with the load balancer, holding at least the AWS managed baseline rule groups and a rate based rule
